title: Workspace Corridor: role-aware sidebar zoning & route affordances
creator: Asha Morgan
description: Problem: As Redwood grows the Console surface has accumulated multiple overlapping navigation affordances (left rail, top crumbs, workspace chips) which confuse role-based workflows (engineer vs. platform admin vs. finance). The current sidebar groups unrelated routes and buries rollout and cost dashboards behind two clicks. Goals: 1) Provide a single, role-aware entry corridor that surfaces the most relevant routes (Dashboards, Rollouts, Cost Views, Model Catalog, Dedicated Pools) at a glance; 2) Reduce click depth to key observability pages (token cost breakdown, per-route latency); 3) Make workspace switching discoverable and undo-able; 4) Preserve compactness for low-vertical-space screens and maintain keyboard navigability and screen-reader semantics. Constraints: must be compatible with existing permission model (RBAC) and the dedicated/private routing layer (smart routing) and not require backend schema changes for routes. Success metrics: reduced mean clicks-to-cost-dashboard from 4 -> 2, decreased time-to-first-rollout-insight by 30%, and positive qualitative feedback from at least 6 customer-facing teams.
acceptance_criteria: Role-aware left rail prototype (desktop + tablet) available in Figma with component tokens and hover/focus states
Working React prototype linked to staging Console that demonstrates: collapsed and expanded rail, workspace switcher modal, and persistent cost-lenses
Design handoff with component specs and ARIA attributes for screen readers
PM sign-off on cognitive load reduction study (3 internal testers) and accessibility audit completion
Implementation plan with ENG team and clear rollout toggles for A/B canary
decisions: Adopt a two-tier rail: primary lanes (role-topics) + secondary contextual row for recent routes and active rollouts
Workspace switcher becomes a persistent affordance in the rail (top-left) and shows last-3 workspaces by default with a search box
Cost and Rollouts get pinned quick-actions (eye icon for cost-lens, rocket icon for rollouts) that open in a right-side micro-panel for fast readouts
Collapsed rail preserves icons-only with tooltips + long-press for touch devices; keyboard users get aria-expanded and route shortcuts
